title: CommandOutput
description: Every document the CLI prints with --json. Scan results (list, show) and check results carry schema_version 1, which changes only on breaking changes.

CaptureFailure.description: What `debug capture --json` prints when nothing was recorded.

tool.description: The tool id that was asked for.

CaptureFailure.title: CaptureFailure

CaptureOutcome.description: What `debug capture --json` prints after writing a capture file.

tool.description: The tool id that was captured.

destination.description: Path of the capture file that was written.

exit_code.description: Exit code of the tool's version command (recorded even when non-zero).

CaptureOutcome.title: CaptureOutcome

CheckResult.description:
The result of `check --json`: one live scan, then every requirement tested against the
active install of its tool. The exit code is 0 exactly when `passed` is true.

schema_version.description: Changes only on breaking changes to this format; the same counter as ScanResult's.

scanned_at.description: When the scan ran, RFC 3339 in UTC.

requirements.description: One entry per requirement, in the order given.

CheckResult.title: CheckResult

FailureOutcome.description: Why nothing was captured. More values may be added without a breaking change; handle unknown ones.

version.description: The version as the tool prints it, vendor suffixes included.

path.description: Absolute path of the executable that was run.

source.description: `path`, or the id of the provider that reported the install.

via.description: The manager whose shim serves this install, or null.

raw.description: Decoded version output the version was parsed from, or null.

RequirementOutcome.description: `passed`: met. Every other value is a failure: `unmet` (the active version is outside the range), `not-comparable` (the active version has no leading number to compare), `missing`, `error` or `timeout` (the tool has no usable active install; same meaning as the tool status). More values may be added without a schema_version bump; handle unknown ones.

RequirementResult.description: The verdict on one requirement given to `check`.

requirement.description: The requirement exactly as given, e.g. `node@>=20`.

tool.description: Tool id the requirement is about.

spec.description: The version spec after `@` (e.g. `>=20,<23`), or null for a presence-only requirement.

version.description: Version of the active install as the tool prints it, or null when there is none.

path.description: Absolute path of the active install, or null when there is none.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of the verdict; not for parsing.

RequirementResult.title: RequirementResult

ScanResult.description:
The result of one live scan: what `list --json` and `show --json` print.

`platform` and `status` may gain values without a schema_version bump; handle
unknown ones (for example with a default branch).

schema_version.description: Changes only on breaking changes to this format.

scanned_at.description: When the scan ran, RFC 3339 in UTC.

tools.description: `list`: every tool known on this OS, missing ones included. `show`: the requested ones.

ScanResult.title: ScanResult

Tool.description: One tool and every install of it that was found.

id.description: Stable tool id, as used on the command line (e.g. `git`).

active.description: The install that runs when you type the command, or null when there is none.

installs.description: Every install found, the active one first.

notes.description: Human-readable explanations for the status (why missing, what failed); not for parsing.

Tool.title: Tool

ToolStatus.description: More values may be added without a schema_version bump; handle unknown ones.
